east kilbride.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit across East Kilbride
s1loc: Loaves and Fishes EK hands out more than 250 food parcels a week along with clothing, toiletries and household items, while the East Kilbride Community Foodbank, run by local churches working together at East Mains Baptist Church, keeps a Monday drop-in going for families in crisis. FareShare moves surplus food from the trade out to community groups across Lanarkshire, and the East Kilbride Community Trust rallies volunteers around sport, health and learning for the town.

The sector here runs at every size. National and regional charities keep shops and central buying behind them, from the British Heart Foundation and Barnardo's Scotland stores to the big research names, while small community groups, foodbanks, pantries and volunteer-run projects work on a shoestring across Westwood, Whitehills, the Murray and Lindsayfield. We are set up to serve the national charity with shops across East Kilbride and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts for the big central buyers and direct online ordering, no minimum, for the smallest volunteer group.

Voluntary Action South Lanarkshire connects helpers to causes town-wide, and Universal Connections runs youth, family and community learning across East Kilbride, with volunteers training as Bikeability leaders. Barnardo's keeps a children's store on Lindsayfield Parade, charity shops cluster through the town centre, and re-established community councils in Westwood pull neighbours together, so the giving runs from a national retail chain right down to a single pantry kept going by volunteers in the Village and Calderwood.

south shields.region: South Shields and Tyne and Wear
south shields.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit across South Shields
s1loc: Hospitality and Hope, founded in 2002 by local church volunteers, runs community shops, the South Tyneside Food Bank and homelessness support across South Shields, while the Key to Life Foodbank feeds families and individuals through a team of volunteers. FareShare moves surplus food from the food industry out to charities and community groups across Tyneside, and Hospitality and Hope keeps a rota of volunteers with transport collecting from donation points town-wide for its food banks and community hubs.

The sector here runs at every size. National and regional charities keep shops and central buying behind them, from the British Red Cross to St Clare's Hospice and the big research names, while small community groups, foodbanks, pantries and volunteer-run projects work on a shoestring across Westoe, Cleadon Park, Whitburn and Boldon. We are set up to serve the national charity with shops across South Shields and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts for the big central buyers and direct online ordering, no minimum, for the smallest volunteer group.

St Clare's Hospice, based in Jarrow and caring for adults south of the Tyne since 1987, runs charity shops in South Shields and at the Viking Precinct in Jarrow, taking donated goods and offering free collection of larger items. South Tyneside Citizens Advice partners with grassroots groups, the Shields Gazette lists donation points town-wide, and church and mutual-aid projects keep emergency food flowing, so the giving runs from a hospice retail chain right down to a single volunteer-run pantry in Hebburn or Cleadon.

burton-on-trent.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit across Burton-on-Trent
s1loc: Burton YMCA, an independent Christian charity supporting homeless people across East Staffordshire, runs a food bank with a part-time coordinator and a team of volunteers, plus three furniture stores selling low-cost white goods and household essentials across Staffordshire and Derbyshire. Burton HOPE, made up entirely of volunteers, hands out three-day emergency food parcels, clothing, toiletries and help obtaining ID, while the Consolidated Charity of Burton upon Trent backs food bank donations and local good causes.

St Giles Hospice runs a superstore on the High Street and a shop on Station Street, taking donated clothing, homewares, electricals and books to fund its care, while a string of charity shops lines the town centre. The Burton Albion Community Trust runs grassroots projects across the borough, and church and mutual-aid groups keep emergency food and clothing flowing, so the giving runs from a hospice retail chain right down to a single volunteer-run parcel pack in Branston or Stretton.

shrewsbury.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit across Shrewsbury

FareShare moves surplus food from the trade out to community groups across Shropshire, and the Shropshire Larder network points people to emergency food right across the county, with most clients referred in through partner agencies.

Church-run projects keep food and encouragement flowing, and grassroots groups rally helpers, so the giving runs from a county-wide retail chain right down to a single volunteer-run pantry in Monkmoor or Meole Brace.

rugby.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit across Rugby
s1loc: Hope4, which began as a soup kitchen in 2005, now runs the Hope Centre for people experiencing homelessness and Rugby Foodbank in the Trussell network, with more than 80 volunteers giving over 10,000 hours a year. In the last year the foodbank handed out over 7,000 parcels, four in ten to children, while the Hope Centre offers food, showers, clean clothing, laundry, health care and housing support to people sleeping rough or sofa surfing.

The Myton Hospices, backed by almost 1,000 volunteers, run shops on Albert Street and Church Street, a furniture store in the Rugby Central Shopping Centre and a Support Hub for anyone living with or caring through a life-limiting illness. Hope4 has won the King's Award for Voluntary Service, Warwickshire County Council backs work on hunger and homelessness, and church and mutual-aid groups rally helpers, so the giving runs from a hospice retail chain right down to a single volunteer-run pantry in Brownsover or Bilton.

Stafford Foodbank, in the Trussell network, feeds local people in crisis, while Signposts Services runs a foodbank at Rising Brook Community Church and Highfields hosts a signpost centre with a cafe and benefit-application help.

taunton.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit across Taunton
s1loc: Taunton Foodbank gives seven-day food supplies to people in crisis, while Taunton Open Door, kept going by a team of volunteers, supported over 200 homeless clients in 2025, served more than 4,200 meals and handed out 4,200 items of clothing. The Somerset Community Foundation funds local causes and inspires giving across the county, and FareShare moves surplus food from the trade out to community groups, with the Samaritans of Taunton and Somerset adding a listening ear town-wide.

The sector here runs at every size. National and regional charities keep shops and central buying behind them, from St Margaret's Hospice Care with its 31 stores to the British Heart Foundation and the big research names, while small community groups, foodbanks, pantries and volunteer-run projects work on a shoestring across Halcon, Priorswood and North Taunton. We serve the national charity with shops across Taunton and the one-room foodbank alike, with trade accounts for the big central buyers and direct online ordering, no minimum, for the smallest volunteer group.

St Margaret's Hospice Care gives free care to anyone facing a life-limiting illness in Somerset, with a hub and in-patient unit in Taunton funded by a chain of charity shops across the county. The North Taunton Partnership runs Priorswood Community Centre with advice surgeries, social groups and youth activities, Citizens Advice Taunton holds clinics at the Halcon Link Centre, and church and mutual-aid groups rally helpers, so the giving runs from a hospice retail chain right down to a single volunteer-run pantry in Halcon or North Taunton.
